title: SRE at Scale: Launching and Running a Service
intro: A new service is launching. Take it through the lifecycle SRE teams at large companies use: a production readiness review, capacity planning, load testing, SLOs and burn-rate alerts, safe progressive rollouts, maintenance that respects disruption budgets, chaos experiments, a real incident, and the postmortem that closes the loop.
resolution: Reliability is designed in, measured, tested, and then defended. The readiness review found the gaps; capacity planning and load tests set the numbers; SLOs defined 'reliable enough'; canaries and PDBs made changes and maintenance safe; chaos tested the assumptions; and when the retry storm came anyway, the postmortem turned it into better defaults. That loop, not any single tool, is what SRE at Google-scale companies is. Finish with the postmortem Writing Lab (yaml-028).
